<STRUCT_0001>
The main application of flat descent for modules is
the corresponding descent statement for quasi-coherent
sheaves with respect to fpqc-coverings.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme.
Let <MATH_0002> be an fpqc covering of algebraic spaces over <MATH_0003>, see
Topologies on Spaces,
Definition <REF_0001>.
Any descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves
for <MATH_0004> is effective.
Moreover, the functor from the category of
quasi-coherent <MATH_0005>-modules to the category
of descent data with respect to <MATH_0006> is fully faithful.

This is more or less a formal consequence of
the corresponding result for schemes, see
Descent, Proposition <REF_0001>.
Here is a strategy for a proof:
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> The fact that <MATH_0001> is a refinement of the trivial
covering <MATH_0002> gives, via
Lemma <REF_0002>,
a functor <MATH_0003> from the
category of quasi-coherent <MATH_0004>-modules to the category of
descent data for the given family.
<STRUCT_0003> In order to prove the proposition we will construct a
quasi-inverse functor
<MATH_0005>.
<STRUCT_0004> Applying again
Lemma <REF_0003>
we see that there is a functor
<MATH_0006>
if <MATH_0007> is a refinement of the given family.
Hence in order to construct the functor <MATH_0008> we may assume that
each <MATH_0009> is a scheme, see
Topologies on Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0004>.
This reduces us to the case where all the <MATH_0010> are schemes.
<STRUCT_0005> A quasi-coherent sheaf on <MATH_0011> is by definition a quasi-coherent
<MATH_0012>-module on <MATH_0013>. Now for any
<MATH_0014> we get an fppf covering
<MATH_0015> by schemes and a morphism
<MATH_0016> of coverings
lying over <MATH_0017>. Given a descent datum
<MATH_0018> we obtain a quasi-coherent
<MATH_0019>-module <MATH_0020> corresponding
to the pullback <MATH_0021> of
Lemma <REF_0005>
to the covering of <MATH_0022> and using effectivity for fppf covering of schemes, see
Descent, Proposition <REF_0006>.
<STRUCT_0006> Check that <MATH_0023> is functorial in <MATH_0024>.
Omitted.
<STRUCT_0007> Check that <MATH_0025> is compatible
with morphisms <MATH_0026> of the site <MATH_0027>, so that
the system of sheaves <MATH_0028> corresponds to a quasi-coherent
<MATH_0029> on <MATH_0030>, see
Properties of Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0007>.
Details omitted.
<STRUCT_0008> Check that <MATH_0031> is quasi-inverse
to the functor constructed in (1). Omitted.
<STRUCT_0009>
This finishes the proof.
